newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee closes low on lack of dlr sales.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee closes low on lack of dlr sales.

text.p: The Sri Lanka rupee closed down on Wednesday as banks were reluctant to sell dollars, despite buying demand for the currency, dealers said.
The rupee closed down at the Central Bank selling level of 59.15, after opening at 59, they said.
"The rupee was pushed down mainly due to a lack of dollar sales by banks, as they see the currency rising more overseas," said an American Express Bank dealer.
"Demand for dollars was fuelled by import covering and banks squaring positions," he said.
The Central Bank pushed up the dollar by eight local cents due to overseas gains on Wednesday. Buying and selling rates were fixed at 57.9794 and 59.1507.
Overnight call money closed at 8.125 percent.
